traceability.evidence:
Story file exists: - docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md (validated via check_file_exists)
Core rule implementation: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Annotated with story 006.0 and requirements REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION (JSDoc at top and per-function comments). - Parses @story annotations from comments: - handleComment(): splits commentNode.value into lines, normalizes them, and passes those starting with "@story" to validateStoryPath(). - validateStoryPath(): extracts the path token from the @story line and delegates to processStoryPath(). - These directly implement **REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION**. - Path resolution and options: - create(context): derives cwd from context.cwd ?? process.cwd and reads options { storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension } with defaults: - storyDirectories: default ["docs/stories", "stories"] - allowAbsolutePaths: default false - requireStoryExtension: default true - Passed through to handleComment/processStoryPath, fulfilling **REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION** and **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS**. - Security validation: - processStoryPath() calls performSecurityValidations({ storyPath, cwd, allowAbsolute, ... }). - If securityOk is false, it aborts further processing, which enforces absolute/path traversal rules per **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**. - Extension enforcement: - When requireExt is true and hasValidExtension(storyPath) is false, it reports messageId: "invalidExtension" with data.path, implementing the .story.md requirement from **Core Functionality** and **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION** (extension aspect). - Existence and error handling: - reportExistenceProblems() calls normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs) then handleProjectBoundaryForExistence() then reportExistenceStatus(). - reportExistenceStatus() distinguishes: - status === "missing" → report messageId: "fileMissing" with { path }. - status === "fs-error" → report messageId: "fileAccessError" with { path, error } derived from the underlying Error or value. - These behaviors satisfy **REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE** and **REQ-ERROR-HANDLING**. - Project boundary enforcement: - reportExistenceProblems() passes candidates and existenceResult into handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(). - If handleProjectBoundaryForExistence() indicates invalidByBoundary, it reports invalidPath and aborts, implementing **REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY** in combination with helpers. - User-facing diagnostics/messages: - meta.messages definitions: - fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found". - invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'". - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'". - fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. Please check file existence and permissions." - All include the offending path and, for filesystem errors, the underlying message, matching **User Experience** and **REQ-ERROR-HANDLING**.
Supporting utilities (file existence, caching, boundary, security): - src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - Story/requirement annotations for 006.0 at top and on each function. - Existence and caching: - fileExistStatusCache: Map caches fs results, directly implementing **REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION**. - checkSingleCandidate(): guarded by try/catch around fs.existsSync and fs.statSync, returning statuses: - "missing" when does not exist or exists but not a regular file. - "exists" when statSync().isFile() is true. - "fs-error" when any exception occurs, with error saved. - getStoryExistence(candidates): - Iterates candidates, returns first status === "exists" with matchedPath when found. - Otherwise, if any candidate had status "fs-error", returns status "fs-error" with representative error. - Else returns status "missing". - storyExists(paths: string[]): wraps getStoryExistence and returns boolean result.status === "exists". - __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests(): clears cache to allow repeated tests with different fs mocks. - These collectively satisfy **REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE**, **REQ-ERROR-HANDLING**, and **REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION**. - Path resolution and boundary: - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - If storyPath starts with "./" or "../", resolves only against cwd. - Otherwise, first resolves cwd+storyPath, then cwd+dir+basename(storyPath) for each dir in storyDirs. - Implements flexible resolution relative to cwd and configured story directories per **REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION** and **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS**. - normalizeStoryPath(): constructs candidates via buildStoryCandidates, gets existence via getStoryExistence, and returns { candidates, exists, existence } for use in rule. - enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd): - Normalizes both cwd and candidate and checks candidate === cwd or candidate.startsWith(cwd + path.sep). - Returns { candidate: normalizedCandidate, isWithinProject } used by helpers to enforce **REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY** and **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**. - Security helpers: - isAbsolutePath(), containsPathTraversal(), isTraversalUnsafe(), hasValidExtension(), isUnsafeStoryPath() implement checks for absolute paths, path traversal, and extensions fulfilling **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**.
Helper module for security and project boundary decisions: - src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - Annotated for story 006.0 and REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS. - analyzeCandidateBoundaries(candidates, cwd): uses enforceProjectBoundary() over all candidates, returning booleans hasInProjectCandidate and hasOutOfProjectCandidate. - handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(options): - If all candidates are out-of-project (hasOutOfProjectCandidate && !hasInProjectCandidate), calls reportInvalidPath(...) and returns true. - If existenceResult.status === "exists" and matchedPath is not within project, reports invalidPath and returns true. - Otherwise returns false. - This logic enforces that only in-project files can ever be considered valid, satisfying **REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY** and **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS** when combined with misconfigured storyDirectories. - performSecurityValidations(options): - If path.isAbsolute(storyPath) and !allowAbsolute → reportInvalidPath(...) and stop further processing. - If path contains ".." or slash/backslash, resolves against cwd and rejects if full path does not start with cwd + path.sep, reporting invalidPath. - Returns boolean to indicate whether downstream checks should proceed. - Implements absolute-path and traversal protections from **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**.
Rule documentation: - docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md - Explicitly references story 006.0 and requirements: - REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION. - Describes behavior: - Prevents absolute paths unless allowed. - Prevents path traversal outside project directory. - Enforces .story.md extension when required. - Resolves candidate file locations in configured story directories. - Distinguishes fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, and fileAccessError. - Details boundary behavior: - Explains how out-of-bounds candidates lead to invalidPath even if the physical file exists. - Clarifies that absolute paths are treated as out-of-bounds by default and only accepted when allowed and within project boundary. - Provides detailed options section for storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension with semantics matching the implementation. - Contains correct and incorrect examples exactly matching the story’s **Path Resolution Examples** and **Configuration Integration**, fulfilling the **Documentation** acceptance criterion. - README.md also lists the rule with short description and link to this doc.
Tests targeting this story/rule (behavioral verification): - tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts (annotated with @story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md and REQ-* IDs) - RuleTester suite "Valid Story Reference Rule (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)": - Valid cases: - "[REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE] valid story file reference": `// @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md`. - "[REQ-EXTENSION] valid .story.md extension": ensures correct extension recognized. - "[REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] valid relative path with ./ prefix": `// @story ./docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Invalid cases: - Missing file: expects messageId "fileMissing" with data.path set to the story path (**REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE**, **User Experience**). - Invalid extension: expects "invalidExtension" with data.path (**Core Functionality**, extension rule). - Path traversal: `// @story ../outside.story.md` → messageId "invalidPath" (**REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**, **REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY**). - Absolute path not allowed: `// @story /etc/passwd.story.md` → "invalidPath" (**REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**). - Additional RuleTester suites for configuration and boundaries: - configurablePathsTester: - Valid: with options { storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"] }, verifies that bare filename `001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` and an explicit docs/stories path are accepted (**REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS**, **REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION**). - allowAbsolutePathsTester: - Valid: when allowAbsolutePaths: true, an absolute path inside project plus a normal docs/stories reference are accepted. - Invalid: when allowAbsolutePaths: false, the same absolute path triggers messageId "invalidPath". - These assert correct allowAbsolutePaths behavior per **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS** and **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**. - relaxedExtensionTester: - With { requireStoryExtension: false }, a .story.md file plus the 006.0 story are accepted and there are no invalidExtension diagnostics, confirming the extension enforcement is configurable (**REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS**). Behavior is consistent with documentation description for relaxing the extension requirement. - projectBoundaryTester: - Constructs an absolute path under a directory outside the project root, with allowAbsolutePaths: true and storyDirectories pointing outside the project. - Expects messageId "invalidPath", confirming that misconfigured storyDirectories cannot cause external files to be treated as valid and that project boundary enforcement works (**REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY**, **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**). - Jest tests under describe("Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries..."): - After each test, cleans up temp dirs, resets existence cache via __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests(), and restores Jest mocks (verifies caching is test-safe, satisfying **REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION** testing concerns). - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] uses storyDirectories when resolving relative paths": mocks fs.existsSync/statSync such that only one candidate path is considered existing and a file; calls runRuleOnCode() asserting diagnostics is an array and no crash. Valid behavior is already asserted via RuleTester; this verifies internal helper interactions and demonstrates use of storyDirectories. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] allowAbsolutePaths permits absolute paths inside project when enabled": ensures the rule processes an absolute path without crashing when allowed. - "[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] storyDirectories cannot escape project even when normalize resolves outside cwd": checks that processing `../outside-boundary.story.md` does not crash and diagnostics are collected; combined with RuleTester above this confirms boundary treatment for outside-project references. - "[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] misconfigured storyDirectories outside project cannot validate external files": mocks fs so an external file appears to exist under a misconfigured external storyDirectories entry, then verifies diagnostics contain at least one with messageId "invalidPath". This explicitly tests **REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY** and **REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION**. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] requireStoryExtension=false accepts existing .md story file": mocks fs for docs/stories/developer-story.map.md, runs with requireStoryExtension: false and storyDirectories ["docs/stories"], and asserts diagnostics include no invalidExtension messages. Confirms extension configurability per **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS**. - Error handling and fs error tests (describe "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling..."): - "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] storyExists returns false when fs throws": - Mocks fs.existsSync and fs.statSync to throw EACCES, asserts storyExists() does not throw and returns false. - Directly validates **REQ-ERROR-HANDLING** behavior of storyExists. - "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] storyExists returns false when fs.statSync throws EIO and existsSync is true": - Mocks existsSync to true and statSync to throw EIO, expects no throw and false, further exercising fs-error handling. - "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] rule reports fileAccessError when fs.statSync throws and existsSync is true": - Mocks existsSync true and statSync to throw EIO, runs rule and verifies diagnostics contain messageId "fileAccessError" with data.error containing "EIO". - Confirms that the rule emits fileAccessError diagnostics with contextual error information per **REQ-ERROR-HANDLING** and **User Experience** criteria. - "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] rule reports fileAccessError when fs throws": - Mocks existsSync and statSync to throw EACCES, runs rule, and asserts fileAccessError diagnostics exist with error message including "EACCES". - Shows permissions-style errors are reported with clear context, matching **REQ-ERROR-HANDLING** and acceptance criteria for filesystem edge cases.
